candidates.background: Schwertner is an orthopedic surgeon from Georgetown. He holds a pharmacy degree from the University of Texas at Austin and a medical degree from the University of Texas Medical Branch in Galveston. He served one term in the Texas House (District 20) before winning the Senate seat in 2012, and he chairs the Senate Business and Commerce Committee.

priorities.text: Campaigns on property tax relief and on housing affordability through infrastructure, financing options and workforce development.
Lists grid reliability, energy emergency preparedness, new power generation and nuclear energy development as priorities.
Says he supports border security funding and tools for law enforcement against cartels and human smuggling.
Says he supports teacher pay increases, career and technical education and parental control in education.
Says water infrastructure and groundwater management reform are needed, including replacing groundwater conservation district boundaries with aquifer-based authorities.

record.text: Joint author of SB 8 (2025), requiring certain sheriffs to enter 287(g) agreements with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement; he moved adoption of its conference report, which passed 20-11.
Voted for SB 2 (2025), creating an education savings account program, and was listed as a coauthor.
Voted for SB 10 (2025), requiring the Ten Commandments to be displayed in public school classrooms, and was listed as a joint author.
Coauthored and voted for SB 3 (2025), which would have banned consumable hemp-derived THC products; Gov. Greg Abbott vetoed it.
Joint author of and voted for SB 17 (2025), restricting land purchases by people and entities tied to certain foreign countries.
Coauthored SJR 5 (2025), a constitutional amendment allowing denial of bail for certain violent offenses, and voted for final Senate approval.
Joint author of and voted for SB 16 (2025), requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote; the bill did not pass the House.
Voted for HB 2 (2025), the school finance bill that passed the Senate 31-0.
Voted for SB 14 (2023), banning gender transition treatments for minors.
Voted for SB 8 (2021), the law banning most abortions after cardiac activity is detected, and was listed as a joint author.
Moved adoption of the conference report on HB 1927 (2021), which allows permitless carry of handguns by adults 21 and older; it was adopted 17-13.
Voted for HB 2127 (2023), which limits city and county regulations in areas covered by state law.
Voted for SB 388 (2025), setting goals for dispatchable generation; it did not pass the House.

notes.text: In December 2018 the University of Texas at Austin closed an investigation into allegations that he sent sexually explicit messages to a graduate student, concluding the available evidence did not support a policy violation; he denied sending the messages. In January 2019 he asked to give up his Health and Human Services Committee chairmanship.
ATPE reports he was endorsed in the 2018 primary by the Texas Home School Coalition PAC and by Texans for Fiscal Responsibility.
Says he has been endorsed by Donald Trump, Greg Abbott and Dan Patrick.
